conversation: Good to see everyone. My family taught me to leave enough fish for next month, and I want this lake supporting our village for years. With 100 tons in the lake, we can each catch 10 tons this month, leaving 50 to double back to 100. That’s $10,000 each per month if we keep to it. Can we agree to that limit and check in together after each month’s catches are revealed? John, what do you think?

I’m in, Luke. My family’s fished this lake for years, and I want our children to have the same chance. I’ll stick to 10 tons, and we can review the catches together each month. If the lake starts a month below 100 tons, let’s agree to lower our limits so it can recover. Kate, does that sound fair to you?

I’m on board with 10 tons each. My family taught me that a good catch should never come at the expense of next season—or our neighbors. If the lake starts below 100 tons, we could split only what’s above 50 tons equally, leaving enough to replenish it. If it’s at 50 or below, we pause fishing to let it recover. Kate, would that work for you?

I’ll commit to 10 tons too. Sharing the catch fairly and leaving 50 tons means dependable income for our families, rather than one big payday followed by an empty lake. Jack’s recovery rule makes sense to me, and we can check everyone’s catches together each month. Kate, are you comfortable with that plan?

That works for me. I’ll take no more than 10 tons this month and follow Jack’s recovery rule if stocks fall. This lake supports our whole village, so if anyone feels pressure to catch extra, let’s talk before fishing rather than put everyone’s future income at risk. We’re all agreed—let’s check in when this month’s catches are revealed.
